target_customer: Governments, legislators, parties and civic groups wanting online deliberation and voting on proposals
problem: Citizens lack a simple way to understand, debate and vote on legislation, so representatives rarely reflect their views.
business_model: Open source nonprofit software (MIT license), no clear revenue model
product_category: Civic tech deliberation and voting platform

founders.name: Guido Vilariño
founders.background_notes: Only founder on the YC page. Wikipedia and press name Santiago Siri, Cristian Douce and Ricardo Rauch as developers in 2012; not confirmed as co-founders by a YC or company page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web app for discussion and voting; the hard parts were identity verification and adoption, not software.

defensibility.rationale: MIT licensed open source, so anyone could copy or fork it; no data or network lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent or acquirer moved; the GitHub README now warns the project is without maintenance.

market_need_then: Argentina's Net Party ran DemocracyOS and received about 21,000 votes (about 1 percent) in Buenos Aires in October 2013, showing activist interest but no sustained paying demand.

branding.name_origin: Suggests an operating system for democracy; no source states the intent.
branding.domain_note: democracyos.org now redirects to an unrelated candy shop site, so the domain was lost; the project points to democraciaos.org.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch (2015), Wired and used by governments and parties as open source; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in civic tech circles through press, but the project is now unmaintained and its domain is gone.

outcome_analysis: DemocracyOS grew out of Argentina's Net Party and joined YC in Winter 2015 as a nonprofit open source platform. No funding was found, the code has seen little activity since 2018, a no-maintenance warning was added around 2020 and the original domain now points to an unrelated site. The cause is not stated publicly; weak paying demand from governments and an open source nonprofit model without revenue are plausible but inferred.
notes: Cause of decline is not public; the failure factors are an inference, not stated by a source. Abandonment date 2018-12-19 and the 2020 README banner come from a forum comment and a search summary of the README. The YC page still lists status Active. democracyos.org redirected to smileyscandy.ca during research and was not followed. No dated competitor source found (LiquidFeedback, Loomio appear only in undated surveys). No funding found, though Crunchbase has a profile that was not readable.
